title: Lazard presentation of flat modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module such that $-\otimes_R M$ preserves short exact sequences of $R$-modules. There exist a small nonempty directed partially ordered set $I$, an $I$-indexed system of $R$-modules $F_i$ with transition maps $F_i\to F_j$ for $i\le j$, and compatible maps $F_i\to M$, such that each $F_i$ is isomorphic to $R^{r_i}$ for some finite integer $r_i\ge0$, and the induced map $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F_i\longrightarrow M$ is an isomorphism of $R$-modules; the colimit is that of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 058G (theorem-lazard), forward direction for flat modules

proof.text: The hypothesis makes $M$ flat in the injectivity sense of [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: for an injection $A\to B$, apply preservation of the short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to B/A\to0$. Its tensor image starts with an injection $A\otimes_R M\to B\otimes_R M$. No converse characterization of flatness is needed.

source.place: Tag 00HB (definition-flat), comparison of the hypothesis with flatness

proof.text: We first extract a finite-relation consequence of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion]. Let $p:R^n\to M$ and let $v=(v_i)\in\ker p$. Write $x_i=p(e_i)$. The relation $\sum_i v_ix_i=0$ is trivial, so the cited statement gives $k$, $y_j\in M$ and $a_{ij}\in R$ with $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ and $\sum_i v_ia_{ij}=0$. Define $A:R^n\to R^k$ by $A(e_i)=(a_{ij})_j$ and $g:R^k\to M$ by $g(e_j)=y_j$. These formulas give $p=gA$ and $A(v)=0$. For any finite list $v_1,\ldots,v_t\in\ker p$, repeat this construction by induction. For $t=0$ take $A=1$ and $g=p$. If $p=g_tA_t$ and $A_t(v_i)=0$ for $i\le t$, apply the one-vector construction to $g_t$ and $A_t(v_{t+1})\in\ker g_t$, obtaining $g_t=g_{t+1}B$. Then $A_{t+1}=BA_t$ still kills the first $t$ vectors and also kills $v_{t+1}$. Thus $p$ factors through a finite free module by a map killing any prescribed finitely generated submodule of its kernel. For a finite set $J$, choose an enumeration giving a linear isomorphism $u:R^n\to R^J$. Apply the construction to $pu$ and the generators $u^{-1}(v_i)$ of $u^{-1}(N)$. If $pu=gA$ and $A(u^{-1}(N))=0$, then $p=g(Au^{-1})$ and $(Au^{-1})(N)=0$, giving exactly the required factorization for $R^J$.

source.place: Tag 058D (lemma-flat-factors-free), finite-relation argument expanded directly from Tag 00HK (lemma-flat-eq)

proof.text: Set $S=M\times\mathbf Z$ and let $P=R^{(S)}$ denote the module of finitely supported functions $S\to R$, with coordinate vectors $e_s$. Define $f:P\to M$ by $f(e_{(m,z)})=m$; it is surjective since $f(e_{(m,0)})=m$. Put $K=\ker f$. Let $E$ be the set of pairs $e=(J,N)$ where $J\subset S$ is finite and $N\subset R^J\subset P$ is the span of a finite list of elements of $K\cap R^J$. Order $E$ by inclusion of both $J$ and $N$ inside $P$. This is a partial order. It is nonempty, containing $(\varnothing,0)$, and directed: $(J\cup J',N+N')$ is an upper bound, and concatenating generators proves the required finiteness of $N+N'$. Each of these generators lies in $K\cap R^{J\cup J'}$, so the upper bound is an object of $E$. All these are sets in a universe containing $R$ and $M$, so $E$ is small. For $e=(J,N)$ put $M_e=R^J/N$ and let $p_e:M_e\to M$ be induced by $f$; this is well-defined because $N\subset K$. Inclusions induce $M_e\to M_{e'}$ for $e\le e'$; the identity, composition and compatibility laws follow from the inclusions and quotient maps.

source.place: Tag 058G (theorem-lazard), directed finite-presentation system in the second and third proof paragraphs

proof.text: The cocone $(M,(p_e))$ is a colimit in the precise sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Indeed let $c_e:M_e\to T$ be any compatible cocone of linear maps. Define a linear map $h:P\to T$ by $h(e_s)=c_{(\{s\},0)}([e_s])$. For every $e=(J,N)$, the arrows $(\{s\},0)\to e$ for $s\in J$ show on coordinate vectors that $h|_{R^J}=c_e q_e$, where $q_e:R^J\to M_e$ is the quotient. If $v\in K$, its support is contained in a finite $J$ and $(J,Rv)\in E$; the preceding equality gives $h(v)=c_{(J,Rv)}([v])=0$. Consequently $h$ descends to a unique linear map $u:M\to T$: set $u(f(v))=h(v)$, which is well-defined since differences of preimages lie in $K$. The formula $h|_{R^J}=c_e q_e$ implies $up_e=c_e$. Uniqueness follows from the objects $(\{(m,0)\},0)$, whose canonical maps hit every $m\in M$. This proves the universal property without assuming a theorem on elementwise module colimits.

source.place: Tag 058G (theorem-lazard), verification of the asserted directed-presentation colimit

proof.text: Fix $e=(J,N)\in E$. Apply the finite-relation construction of step 2, from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion], to $p=f|_{R^J}$ and a finite generating list of $N$. It gives $A:R^J\to F=R^r$ and $g:F\to M$ with $p=gA$ and $A(N)=0$. Choose pairwise distinct $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in S\setminus J$ with $f(e_{s_l})=g(b_l)$, where $b_l$ is the $l$th coordinate vector of $F$. This is possible because each $m\in M$ has the infinitely many labels $(m,z)$ and only finitely many labels are forbidden. Put $J'=J\cup\{s_1,\ldots,s_r\}$ and define $q:R^{J'}\to F$ by $q(e_j)=A(e_j)$ for $j\in J$ and $q(e_{s_l})=b_l$. Its section $b_l\mapsto e_{s_l}$ proves surjectivity. Its kernel $N'$ is generated by the finitely many vectors $w_j=e_j-\sum_l A(e_j)_l e_{s_l}$ for $j\in J$: subtracting $\sum_{j\in J}v_jw_j$ from any $v\in\ker q$ leaves a vector on the new coordinates whose coefficients are $q(v)=0$. Moreover $f|_{R^{J'}}=gq$, so $N'\subset K$, and $A(N)=0$ implies $N\subset N'$. Hence $e'=(J',N')\in E$ and $e'\ge e$. Write $s:F\to R^{J'}$ for the section on the new coordinates. Define $\bar q:R^{J'}/N'\to F$ by $\bar q([v])=q(v)$, which is well-defined since $N'=\ker q$, and define $\bar s:F\to R^{J'}/N'$ by $\bar s(x)=[s(x)]$. We have $\bar q\bar s=1$ since $qs=1$. For $v\in R^{J'}$, $v-sq(v)=\sum_{j\in J}v_jw_j\in N'$, so $\bar s\bar q([v])=[v]$. Thus $M_{e'}=R^{J'}/N'\simeq F$. We have therefore constructed a free finite stage above every $e$, without assuming finite generation of a general submodule of a finite free module.

source.place: Tag 058G (theorem-lazard), free cofinal stage construction and assertions (1)-(3); kernel generators written explicitly

proof.text: Let $I\subset E$ consist of the pairs $e$ for which $M_e\simeq R^r$ for some integer $r\ge0$, with its inherited order. Step 5 makes $I$ cofinal in $E$. It is small and nonempty; for any $i,j\in I$, first take an upper bound $e\in E$ by step 3 and then a free upper stage $k\in I$ by step 5. Thus $I$ is a directed partial order. Restrict $M_e$ and $p_e$ to $I$. To check directly that $M$ is still its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], extend any compatible cocone $c_i:M_i\to T$ to $E$ by setting $c_e=c_i\circ(M_e\to M_i)$ for any $i\in I$ above $e$. Write $t_{ab}:M_a\to M_b$ for the transition map. If $i,j\in I$ both lie above $e$, choose $k\in I$ above $i,j$. Cocone compatibility gives $c_i t_{ei}=c_k t_{ik}t_{ei}=c_k t_{ek}=c_k t_{jk}t_{ej}=c_j t_{ej}$, proving independence. For $e\le e'$, choose $i\in I$ above $e'$; then $c_{e'}t_{ee'}=c_i t_{e'i}t_{ee'}=c_i t_{ei}=c_e$. Taking $i=e$ when $e\in I$ shows that the extension restricts to the original cocone. Any compatible extension must satisfy $c_e=c_i t_{ei}$ for each $i\in I$ above $e$, proving uniqueness. Step 4 supplies a unique $u:M\to T$ inducing the extended cocone, hence the original restricted cocone. Conversely, if $v:M\to T$ induces the restricted cocone, then for $e\in E$ choose $i\in I$ above $e$ and compute $vp_e=vp_i t_{ei}=c_i t_{ei}=c_e$. Thus $v$ induces the extended cocone and equals $u$ by step 4. This proves the restricted universal property in both directions.

source.place: Tag 058G (theorem-lazard), passage to the cofinal subset of free stages with the universal-property argument supplied

proof.text: For $i=(J_i,N_i)\in I$ take $F_i=M_i=R^{J_i}/N_i$ with the transition maps already constructed and the compatible maps $F_i\to M$. By the definition of $I$, each $F_i$ is isomorphic to $R^{r_i}$ for some finite $r_i\ge0$; choose such data for each $i$ if desired. Step 6 says this is a colimit cocone. Any chosen categorical colimit is uniquely isomorphic to $M$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and that isomorphism is its canonical induced map to $M$. This is every clause of the item.
